subject: Clarification: how chat sessions, prompts, and outputs are classified and purged
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nuancehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nuancehealth.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Quick Q: classification & purge window for chat sessions (for our privacy impact assessment)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Our privacy team asked for a short, clear description of what Redwood treats as: (1) request inputs (prompts), (2) model outputs, and (3) session transcripts/streamed buffers — specifically what gets retained by default, for how long, and what evidence we can provide if we need to demonstrate deletion.

Couple of concrete asks:
- Default retention window for request & response pairs in hosted API (no dedicated contract).
- Whether streamed tokens (intermediate fragments during a long-running stream) are treated as logs or ephemeral buffers.
- Where session transcripts live (do they appear in the same store as requests/answers?) and whether they can be auto-purged on shorter timelines.

I'm attaching our procurement checklist so you can see the evidence items the privacy folks will expect. If you can send a small paragraph we can drop into the PIA that would be perfect.

Appreciate it — Sarah

--
Sarah Lin
Privacy & Compliance, Nuance Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nuancehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nuancehealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 17:25:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Quick Q: classification & purge window for chat sessions (for our privacy impact assessment)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the clear list — below is a concise breakdown you can paste into the PIA and a short note on evidence. If you want, we can follow up with a 20-minute call to walk the privacy team through the controls.

Summary (paste-friendly):
- What we treat as a request (prompts): Any user-supplied text or structured input sent to the API is recorded as a request ("prompt" in the PIA). By default, hosted accounts are retained for 60 days from the time of ingestion.
- What we treat as an output (model answers): Final model-generated responses returned to the caller are stored as outputs. These paired request/response records are retained by default for 60 days for hosted customers.
- Streamed tokens / intermediate buffers: Streaming buffers used to construct a response are treated as ephemeral and are not recorded to long-term logs by default. They are kept in transient memory and discarded immediately after the response finalizes; they do not appear in the persisted request/response store.
- Session transcripts / chat logs: If a customer uses a session/chat API (conversation object), the server-side transcript that represents the conversation history is persisted in the same artifact store as request/response pairs and inherits the same default retention (60 days) unless the customer opts into longer archiving via account config.
- KV cache & runtime artifacts: Internal KV caches used to speed inference are ephemeral and not part of persisted logs; they are evicted according to runtime policy and not surfaced to the customer as stored artifacts.

Evidence & erasure path:
- We can provide a deletion certificate and a deletion timestamp range for specific message IDs on request. Evidence bundle (redacted for PII) includes: deletion log entry, job id, and storage bucket lifecycle record.
- For account-level erasure requests (subject to contract and authentication), we run the erasure job across the region of record and provide an audit package (CSV + manifest).

Notes & caveats:
- These are the hosted defaults. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can configure different retention windows and physical residency.
- For EU residency we hold data in the selected region — retention behavior is the same unless contractually changed.

I'll attach a short PDF summary and a link to the erasure request runbook for your team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: redwood-retention-summary.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nuancehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Quick Q: classification & purge window for chat sessions (for our privacy impact assessment)

Adding a couple of security/privacy clarifications for the PIA intake team.

- Residency nuance: For EU customers who select EU region, the persisted request/response store is provisioned in the EU region and lifecycle rules run there. The default timeline (60 days) remains the same unless the contract specifies otherwise. We can provide region-bound deletion evidence (bucket+object lifecycle entries).
- Shorter retention options: We offer a 30-day hosted default as a contract amendment for customers with tighter needs (e.g., certain health or fintech pilots). If Nuance Health needs that, we can include it as a workstream in procurement.
- Attachment & export notes: The deletion evidence we provide does not include the raw model outputs if those were previously exported by users to external systems — in that case the PIA should note downstream export risk.

Sample one-line to include in the PIA (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference retains customer-requested inputs and corresponding model outputs in a secure, region-bound artifact store by default for 60 days; ephemeral streaming buffers are not persisted. Customers may request shorter retention or provide contract language for alternate retention/residency requirements; Redwood provides an audit bundle demonstrating deletion actions upon validated erasure requests."

Ben — FYI on the shortened 30-day option, please flag any pricing implications when you speak with procurement.

-Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
